{{Short description|Russian mathematician (born 1967)}}
{{Family name hatnote|L'vovich|[[Nazarov]]|lang=Eastern Slavic}}
'''Fedor (Fedya) L'vovich Nazarov''' ({{langx|ru|Фёдор (Фе́дя) Льво́вич Наза́ров}}; born 1967) is a Russian [[mathematician]] working in the [[United States]]. He has done research in [[mathematical analysis]] and its applications, in particular in  [[functional analysis]] and [[classical analysis]] (including [[harmonic analysis]], [[Fourier analysis]], and [[complex analysis|complex]] [[analytic function]]s).

== Biography ==
Fedor Nazarov received his Ph.D. from [[Saint Petersburg State University|St Petersburg University]] in 1993, with Victor Petrovich Havin<ref>{{Cite book|chapter=Victor Petrovich Havin, A Life Devoted to Mathematics|doi=10.1007/978-3-319-59078-3_1 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007%2F978-3-319-59078-3_1.pdf|title=50 Years with Hardy Spaces |series=Operator Theory: Advances and Applications |year=2018 |last1=Baranov |first1=Anton |last2=Kisliakov |first2=Sergei |last3=Nikolski |first3=Nikolai |volume=261 |pages=3–66 |isbn=978-3-319-59077-6 }}</ref> as advisor.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Fedor Nazarov - Math Genealogy|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=116208|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project}}</ref> Before his Ph.D. studies, Nazarov received the Gold Medal and Special prize at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad|International Mathematics Olympiad]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Mathematical Olympiad|url=https://www.imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=11951|access-date=2021-03-25|website=www.imo-official.org}}</ref>

Nazarov worked at [[Michigan State University]] in [[East Lansing, Michigan|East Lansing]] from 1995 to 2007 and at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] from 2007 to 2011. Since 2011, he has been a full professor of Mathematics at [[Kent State University]].<ref>[http://www.kent.edu/math/people/~fnazarov/ Homepage of Professor Nazarov at Kent State University] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927084156/http://www.kent.edu/math/people/~fnazarov/ |date=2012-09-27 }}.</ref>

== Awards ==
Nazarov was awarded the [[Salem Prize]] in 1999 "for his work in harmonic analysis, in particular, the [[Fourier transform#Uncertainty principle|uncertainty principle]], and his contribution to the development of [[Bellman function]] methods".<ref>{{cite journal|last=Bourgain|first=J.|author-link=Jean Bourgain|year=1999|title=Nazarov Awarded 1999 Salem Prize|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/199909/people.pdf|journal=Notices Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=46|issue=9}}</ref>

He gave an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited talk at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2010, on the topic of "Analysis".<ref>{{cite web|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url=http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|publisher=[[International Congress of Mathematicians]]|access-date=2013-08-15|archive-date=2017-11-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>
